summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer presented with acute onset of severe vomiting, unable to tolerate oral intake. She had been symptom-free since a prior Botox injection but re-presented after a week of recurrent vomiting. Initial management included IV fluids, antiemetics, and insulin adjustment. An abdominal X-ray ruled out obstruction. An EGD revealed esophageal candidiasis and gastritis; biopsies confirmed active esophagitis and chronic gastritis despite negative fungal staining. She received Botox injection into the pylorus for gastroparesis and was started on fluconazole, pantoprazole, and lisinopril for hypertension. Her symptoms improved, allowing advancement to a soft diet. She was discharged home in stable condition on a revised medication regimen with follow-up planned in gastroenterology and endocrinology.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
